note: He clears the starting-point criteria comfortably. Twenty years of lifting, currently 175 lb, already training kettlebells and visibly dropping body fat — plainly not deconditioned and not gym-averse. Health is not in crisis, and his own framing is textbook good-to-great: 'I'm not in terrible shape... I don't have a specific goal, I just wouldn't mind getting stronger, losing a bit more weight', with technique mastery rather than rescue as the aim. Income is the clear miss — '6,000 is a lot of money, right? Like, we're not all millionaires here', and his reference band for fitness spend is $100-200. The 'successful' criterion cannot be scored at all, and that is itself the finding: the rep never asked what he does for a living. The only occupational signal in 25 minutes is that he sits at a desk all day and got busier after college. Assessing the primary ICP criterion was impossible from this call, and it should not have been.
